definition.text: A strategy of shrinking a society's environmental footprint by moderating its demand for energy, carbon and material-based goods and services.

facts.text: As a goal, it means everyone living a good life within planetary boundaries; as a strategy, it means limiting consumption and production without threatening basic human needs.
The IPCC defines it as policies and daily practices that avoid demand for energy, materials, land and water while providing wellbeing for all within planetary boundaries.
Thomas Princen popularised the term in his 2005 book The Logic of Sufficiency.
Its proponents argue that because of efficiency's limits and rebound effects, demand cannot fall enough unless the energy services societies rely on are themselves questioned.
Together with efficiency and consistency it is one of the fundamental sustainability strategies.
A German study found sufficiency measures could theoretically cut household energy use by 70%.
Wolfgang Sachs's 'Four D's' of sufficiency include decelerating, decentralizing and decommercializing.
Critics share their objection to degrowth: it could hurt growth and raise unemployment; sufficiency savings can also cause indirect rebound effects.

title: Ecological overshoot

definition.text: What happens when the demands placed on an ecosystem exceed its ability to regenerate.

facts.text: Global overshoot occurs when humanity demands more than Earth's biosphere can renew.
William R. Catton Jr.'s 1980 book Overshoot is credited with the term's scientific use for humanity's global impact.
Footprint accounts show humanity has exceeded Earth's regenerative capacity every year since 1970.
A country with a footprint smaller than its biocapacity has an ecological reserve; over 85% of the world's people live in countries in overshoot.
Earth Overshoot Day marks the date each year when humanity's resource use exceeds what Earth can regenerate that year.

title: Ecomodernism

definition.text: An environmental philosophy holding that technology can protect nature and improve human wellbeing by decoupling economic growth from environmental impact.

facts.text: It accepts replacing natural ecosystem services with energy, technology and synthetic solutions when these reduce environmental impact.
A key aim is to use technology to intensify human activity, such as high-yield farming and dense cities, so as to leave more room for wild nature.
In April 2015, 18 self-described ecomodernists published An Ecomodernist Manifesto.
It sets itself apart from ecological economics, degrowth, population reduction and the 'soft energy' path.
Eighteen ecological economists replied with 'A Degrowth Response to an Ecomodernist Manifesto', and critics say it ignores mass extinction and the unequal sides of technological modernisation.

contested_note: Degrowth and steady-state economists, among others, reject ecomodernism's confidence that technology can decouple growth from nature.

definition.text: The amount of a resource a country can use without endangering its continued availability, assuming everyone in the world has an equal share.

facts.text: It requires knowing the maximum sustainable use of every resource, set by sustainable yield or by the environment's capacity to absorb waste, both hard to estimate.
Each resource has its own units, so environmental spaces cannot be added into one national total.
Friends of the Earth Europe promoted it in the mid-1990s, but it has largely been superseded by the ecological footprint, which converts all resource use into land area.

title: Factor 10

definition.text: A policy goal of a tenfold cut in resource use per unit of output, so that economies stay within the planet's carrying capacity.

facts.text: Friedrich Schmidt-Bleek of the Wuppertal Institute first proposed Factor 10 and dematerialization in the early 1990s.
It grew from Factor 4, which aims to cut resource and energy use by 75% by doubling output while halving inputs.
It responds to a UNEP call for a tenfold cut in industrialized countries' resource use so enough is left for developing countries.
Businesses and governments have pursued it through eco-efficiency, design for environment and environmental taxes.
